workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer says the cardholder received the Carlton armchair but it is defective: the frame wobbles and one leg is not properly seated. The issuer also says the merchant has not answered the cardholder's refund request. To defend under Visa 13.3, the merchant must prove all three of the following: (1) its published description of the item; (2) that the delivered item matched that description; (3) either that a return/refund route was offered and the cardholder did not use it, or that the cardholder kept using the item after complaining.

workup.action_justification: Only requirement 1 is satisfied; requirements 2 and 3 need order-specific records (correspondence log, unit inspection evidence) that the merchant may be able to supply.
evidence_to_request: Complete customer-contact log for this order: all emails to returns@havenhome.example and any customer-service tickets or calls from the cardholder, with dates and any merchant replies.
Any message sent to the cardholder offering the free collection/repair/replace/refund route, with the send date.
A pre-dispatch QC or inspection record for the specific unit (serial/batch number if available) confirming the frame and legs were secure.
Additional delivery or dispatch photos showing the legs and frame from other angles, if taken.
Any evidence the cardholder kept using the chair after raising the complaint, or declined an offered collection or repair.
workup.rationale: The merchant's listing snapshot of 15 April 2025 documents the Carlton Mid-Century Armchair as sold, including a beech frame and tapered solid oak legs, delivered fully assembled. The only delivery evidence is a driver's front-view photo from 18 April 2025. It confirms a sage armchair was delivered but does not show the frame or leg seating the cardholder disputes. The merchant has supplied its returns policy but no record of contact with this cardholder. So it is unproven whether a return or repair route was offered or declined, and the issuer states the refund request went unanswered. The case is on hold pending the merchant's customer-contact records and unit inspection evidence.
caveats: The issuer says the merchant did not respond to a refund request. If the merchant's inbox shows an unanswered request, requirement 3 cannot be met and liability should be accepted.
Delivery was 18 Apr 2025, so the policy's 7-day defect window ran to about 25 Apr 2025. Check the dates of any cardholder contact against that window.
The listing includes an allen key 'for leg re-tightening if required during transit'. This suggests loose legs are a known issue, but it does not prove the chair was not defective.
In the photo the legs appear dark brown, while the listing says 'Tapered solid oak legs'. Confirm this is a lighting or photo artefact and not a finish mismatch.
The clean AVS/CVV/3DS results and matching postcodes confirm the cardholder's involvement but are irrelevant to a not-as-described/defect claim.

rule_text:
Visa 13.3 - Not as Described or Defective Merchandise
Issuer claim: Cardholder received the goods but they are materially not as described or defective.
Logic: ALL 3 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. The merchant's published description of the item the cardholder purchased
  2. Evidence the item delivered matches that description (photos, specs, serial number match)
  3. Evidence the merchant offered a return/refund route and the cardholder did not use it, OR evidence the cardholder used and retained the merchandise after raising the complaint
prechecks: AVS: Y (full address match); CVV: M (match); 3DS: authenticated
Chargeback raised 23 days after the transaction
